questions.prompt: Sidra's creatinine median is 89.9 and Ufuq's is 1.00. Both columns are numeric and complete. What is the most likely explanation, and what follows?
options: Ufuq's patients have healthier kidneys; pool the values as they are
Ufuq reports mg/dL; confirm with Ufuq and write the factor 88.42 into the contract
One of the columns is corrupt; drop creatinine from the study
The medians differ by chance; compare means instead
questions.explanation: A ratio near a known unit factor points to a unit difference; the producer confirms it and the contract states the conversion for every consumer.
misconceptions: Reads a unit difference as a clinical difference
Discards a usable field instead of asking the producer
Treats an 88-fold difference as sampling noise

questions.prompt: Rawdah's diagnosis codes look like i50.9 and Ufuq's like I509. A colleague joins all three extracts to a diagnosis lookup on the raw code. What happens?
options: The join fails with an error, so the problem is found at once
Only codes in the lookup's exact format match, so most Ufuq and Rawdah rows drop out silently
The database ignores case and dots, so all rows match
Every row matches, some to the wrong diagnosis
questions.explanation: An inner join on codes that were not normalised drops what does not match exactly, without any error; the contract's format rule prevents it.
misconceptions: Expects a silent mismatch to raise an error
Assumes joins normalise text
Confuses missed matches with wrong matches

questions.prompt: Ufuq's latest delivery passes every column rule, but its newest admission is nine days before the delivery date. The contract allows two. What should the gate do?
options: Block the delivery and ask Ufuq to send a complete extract again
Accept it: every row is valid
Accept it and fill the missing days with the average of earlier days
Accept it and note the gap in the study's limitations
questions.explanation: Freshness is a contract clause: a delivery that stops early biases pooled rates, so the gate blocks it and the producer sends it again.
misconceptions: Treats completeness of a period as a property of single rows
Invents data to hide a gap
Lets a known bias into the pooled rate when a new delivery is possible

questions.prompt: Which clause belongs in the shared contract rather than in one consumer's pipeline code?
options: The colour scheme of the study's dashboard
The study's model settings
Ufuq's mapping of discharge codes 1 to 4 onto HOME, TRANSFER, DIED and LAMA
The name of the notebook that reads the feed
questions.explanation: Code maps define what the producer's values mean; written in the contract, every consumer applies the same meaning and a change to it is versioned.
misconceptions: Mixes a consumer's presentation choice with the feed's meaning
Puts an analysis choice into the producers' agreement
Confuses a consumer's file with the contract

questions.prompt: Producers will send HMAC-SHA-256 of the normalised national identifier. Who should hold the key?
options: The consortium's analysts, so they can check matches
Nobody: generate it once and delete it
Each producer its own key
A linkage unit outside the analysis team, which gives the producers one key for this project
questions.explanation: The producers need one shared key to produce matching pseudonyms; keeping it away from the analysts keeps the pseudonyms irreversible for them, and a key per project prevents joins across projects.
misconceptions: Gives the people who see the data the means to re-identify it
Producers need the same key to compute matching pseudonyms
Different keys give different pseudonyms, so nothing links

questions.prompt: Adding a second linkage key on name, birth date and sex raised recall from 0.993 to 1.000 and lowered precision from 1.000 to 0.988. What should you report?
options: Only the recall: the study needs every readmission
Both numbers with counts: 14 pairs recovered, 24 strangers merged, and a proposed rule to filter them
Only precision: wrong links are unacceptable
Neither: the truth file is synthetic, so the numbers mean nothing
questions.explanation: Linkage makes two errors that bias the study in different directions; the decision needs both, as counts as well as rates.
misconceptions: Hides the merged histories the second key created
Hides the readmissions the first key misses
Rejects measurement because the data is synthetic, when the planted truth is exactly what makes it measurable

questions.prompt: Ufuq replaces column Creatinine_mgdl by Creatinine, whose median is 89.3 where the old one was 1.00. How does the policy classify it?
options: Additive: a new column appeared
No change: the same measurement under a clearer name
Breaking: a renamed column and a unit change; a new major version
Breaking only if the data protection officer objects
questions.explanation: The values show the same measurement in a new unit: a rename and a unit change, both breaking, so the contract moves to a new major version.
misconceptions: Reads the schema diff and not the values
Misses the unit change hidden by the rename
Confuses the approvers with the classification

questions.prompt: Why is a new value in a closed code set (Ufuq's discharge code 5) treated as breaking?
options: The study's mapping does not know it, so those rows become null or drop out
Any change to a producer's system is breaking
New codes always mean worse data quality
It is not: new values are always additive
questions.explanation: A consumer with a closed list cannot place the new code, so its rows silently leave the analysis; the producer must announce it.
misconceptions: Over-classifies changes that consumers do not notice
Judges the value instead of its effect on consumers
Ignores that consumers with closed lists lose the rows
